questions.q: Who was Harshavardhana and where was his capital city located?
questions.a: Harshavardhana was a 7th-century ruler of northern India. His capital was at Kanauj. A wrong answer suggests the student is confusing him with earlier emperors like Ashoka or Gupta rulers.

questions.q: Why is Harshavardhana’s rise to power considered to be under "difficult circumstances"?
questions.a: He inherited a small, unstable kingdom after the tragic deaths of his father and elder brother. If a student says "he was born into a large empire," they have missed the key point about his personal struggle to build his kingdom from scratch.

questions.q: If you were a poet living in Harsha’s kingdom, why would you feel supported by him?
questions.a: Steps: 1. Identify Harsha’s traits (patron of arts). 2. Recognize he was a poet himself. 3. Conclude he would appreciate and fund creative work. 4. Explain the benefit of royal patronage. If a student mentions only his army, they fail to apply the concept of his cultural legacy.

questions.q: How does being a "patron of learning" differ from being a "conqueror"?
questions.a: A conqueror focuses on territorial expansion, while a patron invests in schools, scholars, and books. A student who conflates these two misses the specific character of Harsha's reign, which focused on intellectual growth alongside governance.

questions.q: Was Harsha only interested in his own religion? Justify your answer.
questions.a: No, while he was a Buddhist, he supported other faiths and traditions. This shows his inclusive approach to governance. A student failing to see this misses the historical record of his religious tolerance.

questions.q: Imagine you are an advisor to Harsha. What would you suggest he focus on to maintain peace in his empire?
questions.a: A good answer focuses on diplomacy, fair laws, and supporting arts to keep the public happy. A poor answer would focus only on "building bigger walls" or "fighting more," ignoring his diplomatic and cultural style of leadership.
